title: open state and accessible dialog naming
learningObjectives: Explain open state and accessible dialog naming and choose an appropriate native HTML interaction.

understand.concept: The dialog open state indicates whether a dialog is displayed. A dialog should have an accessible name, commonly through aria-labelledby referencing a visible heading, or aria-label when an appropriate visible heading is not available. Modal dialogs should communicate their purpose clearly.
understand.whyItMatters: A named dialog helps screen-reader users understand the context after it opens. Keep the title and instructions visible and ensure the close action has an understandable label.
understand.analogy: A dialog name is the heading on a room's door: it tells users what conversation they have entered.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual dialog, disclosure, and focus behaviour follows HTML and accessibility platform rules.

explain.narrative: The aria-labelledby relationship gives the dialog its accessible name from the visible heading.

practise.guidedTask: Add a descriptive heading and accessible name to a dialog. Inspect the accessibility tree and test with a screen reader where available.
practise.independentTask: Build an interaction using native HTML first. Test keyboard operation, accessible naming, focus behaviour, and browser support.

questions.prompt: What attribute can connect a dialog to its visible heading for its accessible name?
questions.explanation: aria-labelledby references the element or elements that provide the accessible name.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between native and custom widgets?
options: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
Whether a custom widget looks more decorative
Whether ARIA can replace all HTML semantics
questions.answer: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
questions.explanation: Native controls are usually the safer choice unless the interaction genuinely requires custom behaviour.
